text: APC/C with cofactor Cdh1 degrades cell-cycle proteins in late mitosis and G1. Cdh1-null embryos die at E9.5–E10.5 from trophoblast endoreduplication defects and placental malfunction; placental Cdh1 expression rescues lethality. Cdh1-deficient cells proliferate poorly and accumulate numeric and structural chromosomal aberrations, so Cdh1 maintains genomic stability. Cdh1 heterozygotes show increased spontaneous tumour susceptibility (haploinsufficient tumour suppression) and behavioural defects linked to neural stem-cell proliferation. Separately, restoring normal protein synthesis in Emu-Myc/+ mice via ribosomal protein heterozygotes suppressed Myc oncogenicity: Myc-driven synthesis increases cell size and accelerates cell-cycle progression independently of transcriptional targets, while normal synthesis permits programmed cell death to eliminate precancerous cells. Aberrant cap-dependent translation impairs the IRES-dependent mitotic switch, reducing IRES-dependent Cdk11 (Cdc2l/PITSLRE) and causing cytokinesis defects, centrosome amplification and genome instability—reversed by restoring translational control.
